title: Or Rather, Let Me Put It Another Way
title_ar: أو بالأحرى، خليني أقولها بطريقة تانية
gist_ar: نص عن الطلاقة: التصحيح الذاتي والاستطراد علامات كفاءة، مش ضعف.
text:
There is a persistent belief among advanced learners that fluency means never
stopping. The point I'm making is close to the opposite, and it is worth
elaborating rather than asserting.

Consider what a proficient speaker actually does. They signpost — "to return to
your first question" — which allows a listener to survive a digression of thirty
seconds without losing the thread. They correct themselves openly: "the policy
was introduced in 2011, or rather it was drafted in 2011 and introduced two years
later." And having said that, they recap at intervals, not because they have
forgotten but because they can hear that the listener might have.

None of this is smooth. Transcribed, it looks repetitive. What it is, is
coherent, and coherence is what the descriptors reward. Spontaneity without
signposting produces speech that is easy to produce and hard to follow, which is
the failure mode of the confident learner. Long-winded is not the opposite of
succinct; both can be perfectly coherent, and both can fail.

To sum up — and in a nutshell this is the whole argument — the ability to hold
the floor is not the ability to keep talking. It is the ability to keep a
listener oriented while you think. Paraphrase, clarify, digress and consolidate:
these are load-bearing, and a speaker who has none of them is not fluent but
merely quick.

What I mean is this, and bear with me because it sounds like a paradox. The most
eloquent people you know are the ones you have most often heard say "let me put
it another way". They are not struggling. They have simply noticed something you
did not say, and they are the only kind of speaker who ever does.

questions.q: What is the writer's central claim about fluency?
questions.q_ar: إيه ادعاء الكاتب الأساسي عن الطلاقة؟
options: Fluency means speaking continuously without pausing, which is the writer's whole thesis
Fluency is keeping a listener oriented while you think

questions.q: What does the writer call the failure mode of the confident learner?
questions.q_ar: إيه الخطأ اللي بيقع فيه الدارس الواثق؟
options: Spontaneity without signposting — easy to produce, hard to follow

questions.q: Why does a proficient speaker recap?
questions.q_ar: ليه المتحدث المتمكن بيلخّص من وقت للتاني؟
options: Because they have forgotten what they said
Because the assessment descriptors formally require a recap at fixed intervals
Because they can hear that the listener might have lost it

questions.q: What does the writer imply about people who say 'let me put it another way'?
questions.q_ar: إيه اللي الكاتب بيلمّح له عن اللي بيقولوا 'خليني أقولها بطريقة تانية'؟
options: They are struggling to find words
They have noticed a misunderstanding, which is a mark of skill
